question: Of the following pairs of surface molecules, what is used by the virgin T lymphocytes to extravasate to the lymph node?
analysis: Virgin T lymphocytes, also known as naive T cells, use specific surface molecules to home to lymph nodes. The chemokine receptor CCR7 and the adhesion molecule L-selectin (CD62L) are crucial for this process. CCR7 binds to chemokines CCL19 and CCL21, which are expressed in high endothelial venules (HEVs) of lymph nodes, guiding the T cells to these sites. L-selectin facilitates the initial rolling interaction of T cells on the HEVs, allowing them to extravasate into the lymph node. Therefore, the correct pair of surface molecules used by virgin T lymphocytes to extravasate to the lymph node is CCR7 and L-selectin.
